w:r.w:t: All 11 projects, in full — problem, research & decisions, build, outcome, what I'd do differently and client testimonial. Sections without confirmed info are marked in orange as placeholders to fill in by hand. Source content otherwise matches what's live on the portfolio site.
A VR/AR studio with Olympics Committee–level client work, undersold by a website that explained none of it.
End-to-end website design, brand identity, developer management
Full WordPress rebuild, brand identity, pitch deck, social & presentation assets

Visual UniVRs builds VR/AR experiences and graphics good enough to land the Olympics Committee as a client reference — but their website did nothing to earn that kind of trust from a new visitor. Technical, niche services, presented with no real structure or proof.

I started with a two-hour briefing covering target audience, key propositions, services, and the technology itself — dense enough that most of the value came from getting these details right before any design work began.

— Mapped realistic-to-rank keywords against the ones most likely to bring leads, then studied 5–10 top competitors' structure, content and design — not to copy, but to see what had already been tested.
— Packaged the research into a takeaways document, so the client left with marketing and growth insight beyond just a new website.
— Built structure and content flow first, prioritizing clear navigation so a technical service stayed easy to follow.
— Presented a few style/layout directions before building the rest of the site, so the final design matched the brand and vision the client actually wanted.

Designed the remaining pages in the chosen direction, then adapted everything for tablet and mobile. I hired and managed a WordPress developer to build it — including replacing an underperforming developer partway through to keep the project on track. After launch, we added a blog with the client's SEO specialist, plus social covers, a presentation, and a Calendly booking page design.
Of team-wide work from new clients found via the site
Client-reported, based on projects won after launch — no paid ads running at the time.

The developer swap cost real time I hadn't planned for. Next time, I'd run a small paid trial task before committing a multi-month build to a new developer, instead of discovering the fit problem after work was already underway.

“We're already seeing results — even without running ads yet. The website secured us several large projects, giving the whole team six months of work. Clients told us they chose us because of the strong team and portfolio they found through the site. Our average project value has increased nearly 2×, which was our main goal — to strengthen our brand image. As a digital business card, it's working perfectly.”
A pre-seed robot that dusts data centres, pitching investors on a brand and website that didn't exist yet.
Brand identity, website design & build, pitch deck
Brand identity from scratch, Figma Sites build, investor pitch deck, adaptive design
Live site used in investor pitching

iData's founder had engineering, an MVP, and a robot that dusts data centres — a job normally done by people — but nothing to show an investor. No brand, no website, no way to explain the idea visually in a pitch room.
— Built the full brand identity from scratch — palette, type, visual language — with nothing existing to start from.
— Took the founder's 3D model, posed and rendered it for marketing use, since there was no product photography possible yet.
Built to present, not just to look at
— Built the site directly in Figma Sites so it was a real, live, responsive link the founder could put in front of investors — not just a mockup.
— Added custom illustrations alongside the renders to explain the technical concept simply.
Designed and built fully adaptive layouts for desktop, tablet and mobile, and put together the accompanying investor pitch deck in the same visual system.
Site used directly in investor pitches
Outcome of the fundraise itself unconfirmed — contact ended after delivery.

A recruitment agency with clients across two continents and no website at all.
Webflow build, CMS-driven jobs board, brand identity
MarGuru places IT specialists from post-Soviet countries and Europe into Israeli companies — real, ongoing business, but no website at all, which made the agency harder to trust at first contact.
— Ran a briefing interview to find what actually differentiated the agency from larger, more established competitors.
— Researched the recruitment industry and competitor sites to inform structure and messaging.
— Set up a collection so each job posting generates its own page from a simple entry — no manual page-building needed going forward.
— Connected a file-upload plugin so candidates could apply and attach documents directly through the site.
Designed the site from scratch in Figma, then built it in Webflow — my first Webflow project — including the CMS collection and upload-enabled application forms.
Went from no website to a full working site
Client can add jobs herself, no designer needed

Full site redesign, Figma component system, social & dashboard graphics, sister-brand logo
Live, full component system handed over

Square Circle works with some of the biggest names in UK safety and compliance, but their site was built from a generic template and did nothing to prove it — no real structure, no sense of their actual portfolio, no brand presence to speak of.
— Interviewed the owner directly, then mapped where their existing marketing funnel was leaking — and where structure changes could recover it.
— Benchmarked against other compliance and safety providers to see how the strongest ones built trust and presented credentials.
— Built a full Figma system — headers, footers, repeatable blocks — so the design would stay consistent as more pages and campaigns got added.
— The client had almost no usable photography or project imagery at launch. Structured the design to work cleanly with placeholders, then dropped in real assets once the client supplied them.

Designed the full structure, prototype and adaptive layouts, then handed over a complete Figma component system the client's team could keep extending. Also designed a logo for one of their sister brands, plus social and client-dashboard graphics.

A religious lifestyle brand with real assets and ambition, but no consistent visual system across Instagram, email or their companion app.
Social system, email design system, app website design & build
~15 posts + stories shipped monthly, on one system

Sacred & Divine — candles, jewellery, fragrances, and a free companion app with prayers and guided content — had brand assets but no consistency across channels: inconsistent text placement, clashing colors, and an Instagram feed that didn't read as one brand.
— Fixed where and how text sits on every post, so the feed reads as consistent even across dozens of one-off announcements.
One AI art style for recurring content
— Developed a consistent AI oil-painting illustration style for recurring holiday and devotional posts, kept separate from product photography.
— Built reusable header, footer and selling-block components in Figma so campaigns ship without redrawing anything each time.
— Designed and built the companion app's landing page in Wix with a new Figma design system, structured around the app's actual benefits.

Delivered a consistent visual system across Instagram, email and the app's website, producing around fifteen posts and stories a month plus matching email campaigns — all from reusable components rather than one-off design work.

A biodegradable-glove product with a target customer and nothing else — no store, no photography, no way to sell it.
Full Shopify build, AI product photography, benefit graphics, brand positioning
Store launched, ready to advertise on day one

The client had a product — biodegradable gloves aimed at mothers doing everyday household tasks — and almost nothing else. No store, no usable photography beyond a few boxes shot on a white background, and no clear way to present why the product was worth buying.
— All the client gave me was who'd use it and how. Built the visual positioning and messaging from that alone.
— Generated AI product photography and a short use-case video, since there was no real photography to work with.
— Designed graphics explaining why the product beat alternatives, rather than relying on copy alone to make the case.
Ready to sell, not just ready to look at
— Set up the full tagging, product and review system so the client only had to advertise — nothing left to build.

Selected and customized the Shopify template, then built out the full store — product organization, purchase flow, and every piece of supporting content — from a single-sentence brief and no existing assets.

An art therapy startup with just an idea, needing an MVP that felt like therapy through art — not like software.
Digital identity from scratch, illustration direction, MVP website design
MVP shipped; most creative project to date
The founder had an idea for an art-therapy product and nothing built around it yet — no visual identity, no direction for how a wellness product about art should actually look and feel.
Delegated the logo, owned everything else
— Handed logo creation to a specialist, then built the full digital identity around it from scratch.
— Sourced and hand-combined stock illustration into one flowing collage style — done entirely by hand, before AI tools existed to help with this kind of work.
Let the visuals carry the meaning
— Designed the site so the artistic, collage-led look communicated 'this is about art and therapy' without needing much explanatory copy.
Designed the full MVP around the collage illustration style, built out as a working prototype for the founder to develop further.

A DTC dog-nutrition brand with a strong existing design system, testing which campaign approach actually sold subscriptions.
Campaign & A/B variant design, supporting graphics
Note: Framed honestly as work done within someone else's existing design system, not an original build.

Interstellar already had a strong Figma design system in place and knew the site worked — what they needed was speed: new campaign and subscription-selling variants to test against it, without waiting on the original design team.
— Rather than redesigning, executed new campaign pages and A/B variants within the established Figma system — matching, not replacing, what was already working.
— Flagged structural and color suggestions where testing data pointed to a likely improvement, without disrupting the core system.
— Created supporting AI-generated graphics for campaigns that didn't have supplied imagery.
Designed and delivered multiple campaign and A/B test variants within the client's existing system, including one full page designed independently in the established style.
Valued specifically for speed and responsiveness
Client-reported; the brand is no longer operating.

A social and email marketing agency running 30+ client accounts entirely in Photoshop, with no shared system and no Figma.
Figma rollout, component system, social & email campaigns across 30+ accounts
System still in use after she left

Onik Lab ran social and email campaigns for 30+ clients across different industries, but the whole studio worked file-by-file in Photoshop with no shared system — slow, inconsistent, and hard to scale as the client list grew.
— Brought Figma into an agency that had never used it, and built out how the team would actually work in it.
— Created the studio's first reusable component system — buttons, blocks, footers — so campaigns didn't need to be redrawn from scratch for each client.
— Collaborated closely with a copywriter and a Klaviyo specialist across dozens of accounts, keeping design consistent across very different brand voices.
Designed social and email campaigns across 30+ client accounts spanning multiple industries, using the component system to keep quality consistent while working at volume.

A social marketing agency pairing professional photography with design, running continuous Instagram feeds for 20+ clients.
Continuous-feed Instagram design across 20+ client accounts
Sharpest growth period in her visual design skill

DWL Vision's clients — including multi-location hospitality brands — had strong photography from in-house photographers, but needed that photography turned into cohesive, 'continuous feed' Instagram grids where every post visually connected to the next.
— Worked from photographer-supplied shots rather than generating imagery, adding graphic elements that made each post connect to its neighbors.
Every post had to mean something
— The creative director pushed for concept in every single post, not just consistent style — a much higher bar than volume social work usually asks for.
— Went through repeated, demanding rounds of feedback per client — the fastest her visual skills improved at any point in her career.
Designed continuous-feed Instagram campaigns for 20+ clients from different industries, working directly from photographer-supplied content under a demanding, concept-first creative direction.
